pattern.crimePattern: old cattle broker kills the trader who took his life savings for forty cattle that never existed, sold on forged movement permits
pattern.notes: Fictional traders, broker and market staff. Livestock movement permits and county vet stamps are given in outline; the cultural reader is asked to check Narok market practice. The victim is the fraudster.

ob.reportedBy: Nelson Kipkurui, weighing-shed clerk, Narok cattle market
ob.text: The weighing-shed clerk at Narok cattle market reports a livestock trader, Abdirizak Hassan (52), found dead at 18:40 in holding pen 6 after Tuesday's market.

facts.text: Abdirizak Hassan was found dead in holding pen 6 at Narok cattle market at 18:40, after Tuesday's market.
He lies on his back in pen 6. There are no trampling marks on him.
His satchel is still across his chest with KSh 46,000 inside.
Abdirizak's ledger, unfolded: "K. Sigei — 1,600,000" sits in the column headed "Received". The header names his partner, O. Dahir.
Movement permits in his satchel for "40 head, Kajiado → Narok", stamped "COUNTY VETERINAY OFFICER", misspelled.
Dr. Chelimo: her office issued no permits for 40 head from Kajiado this month. Her genuine stamp is spelled correctly and has a different border.
Dr. Chelimo was at the vet office and then in meetings at the county offices next door from 14:00 to 19:00.
Records, Abdirizak's PesaPap: KSh 900,000 received from KIPKORIR SIGEI, and cash deposits of 700,000 the same week.
Records, Abdirizak's PesaPap: KSh 4,000 paid to Till 880 214, MVUA HOLDINGS.
The Mvua payment's memo reads: "stamp: county vet".
Nelson: at about 16:30 he saw Kipkorir and Abdirizak go into the tea hotel's back room. Kipkorir carried "his iron, wrapped in a sack".
Nelson was at the weighing shed all afternoon; its ticket book has his stamp every few minutes.
Nelson: the market closed at 18:00 and the pens emptied as the lorries loaded.
The tea hotel's back room: two chai glasses, one broken; a dark patch scrubbed on the earth floor; drag marks to the back door and the pens' lane.
Kipkorir's branding iron: the brand "KS", scorched old, wiped clean.
Lorry park manifests: Omar loading two lorries from 15:30 to 18:00, signing each one.
Mzee Kasaine: Nancy served tea in the front room all afternoon. "She never left the kettle."
Market fee receipts: Abdirizak's fees paid in full on Tuesday.
Autopsy: a heavy blow from an iron bar with a flat, shaped end. No trampling injuries.
Autopsy: he lay on his back in a narrow place for a while, then was moved.
Autopsy: death between 16:30 and 17:30.
Autopsy: a sound heart.
Lab: Abdirizak's blood in the shaped head of the branding iron.
Kipkorir: "I left the market at two o'clock and went home."
Kipkorir: "Abdirizak owed me cattle."
Kipkorir: "Forty head. My whole life. He laughed. He told me to go to court. I'm sixty-seven, Detective. I haven't got time for court."
Nancy: "My back room was locked all afternoon."
Nancy: she rented the back room to them for KSh 500. She isn't licensed to rent rooms and was afraid.
Omar: "I was loading lorries."
Omar: "He told me he'd sold cattle from Kajiado. We have no cattle in Kajiado."

topics.reply: Nelson sees everything. ...Here. Take it. It's in the sack.

topics.reply: Ask Mzee Kasaine. He sits in that corner from noon. I never left the kettle.

interrogations.intro: Omar doesn't look up from his clipboard. "I was loading lorries."

topics.reply: Forty head from Kajiado? He told me he'd sold cattle from Kajiado. We have no cattle in Kajiado. ...We fought about a lorry, yes. Lorries, not this. Read my manifests.

interrogations.intro: Dr. Chelimo puts her stamp beside the permit. "Look at the spelling. Then look at the border."
Nelson leans in the weighing-shed door. "Half past four. Old Kipkorir and the Somali trader, into Nancy's back room."

proof.concludes: Abdirizak received KSh 1.6 million from Kipkorir for forty cattle that didn't exist, using forged permits. The victim was the fraudster.
Kipkorir didn't go home at two: at 16:30 he went into the tea hotel's back room with Abdirizak, carrying his branding iron.
The killing happened in the back room, rented for KSh 500; the body lay there, then was dragged to pen 6. He died between 16:30 and 17:30.

The branding iron carries Abdirizak's blood. In the tea hotel's back room, Kipkorir Sigei struck Abdirizak with a cattle branding iron, because Abdirizak had taken his life savings for forty cattle that didn't exist.

eliminations.why: He lay somewhere narrow first, the drag marks lead from the back room, and there's no trampling.
Nelson was in the weighing shed all afternoon and saw them go into the tea hotel.
The vet office was full of staff; the scrubbed floor is in the back room.
Omar and the loaders were at the lorry park; the drag marks run from the back room.
Nancy served tea in the front room all afternoon.

Nelson was at the weighing shed, stamping tickets.
Dr. Chelimo was at the vet office and the county offices all afternoon.
His satchel and KSh 46,000 were still on him.
A shaped iron end, not a hoof.
A sound heart; a blow killed him.
The money went the other way: "Received".
That quarrel was Omar's, and he was at the lorry park.
The rent is Nancy's fear, not a reason to kill.

reconstruction.text: Abdirizak sells Kipkorir forty head of cattle "from Kajiado, delivery Tuesday" and takes KSh 1.6 million, most of the old broker's savings. The permits are forged with a fake county vet stamp, bought from Mvua's "document services".
Tuesday. No lorry comes. Kipkorir has brought his branding iron to brand his new herd.
16:30. They meet in the back room of Mama Nancy's tea hotel, rented for KSh 500. Abdirizak laughs and tells him to go to court.
Kipkorir strikes him with the branding iron. A chai glass breaks.
At dusk he drags Abdirizak out of the back door into the emptying pens, scrubs the floor, and goes home. At 18:40 Nelson finds him in pen 6.

clockPlan.note: One records request, on the victim's line. No detention: Kipkorir hands over the iron himself. The trace takes 12 h.
